gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states that Apple lists the M2 MacBook Air as supporting one external display, which means a driver-free extender that adds two screens can light only one of them on that laptop.
standout_why: Compared against theofficejournal.com's under-$150 page (rank 1 in both chats), dejaflow.com (rank 5 and 7) and twelvetabs.com (rank 6 and 8), all opened 2026-11-21. Theofficejournal says single-cable use needs DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt, else HDMI plus USB power, but names no driver and no per-laptop display count. Dejaflow gives fit ranges and flags DisplayLink on the SideTrak Slide, then calls extenders plug-and-play 'for Mac and Windows'. Twelvetabs flags DisplayLink on one pick. None gives a MacBook chip limit. deskfinds.com (rank 4) returned HTTP 403, so it is unchecked, and I did not open theofficejournal's other pages. ChatGPT's own answer already hints at 'MacBooks with external display limitations' without a figure, so the general idea is not new; the Apple figure and its consequence for two-screen extenders are.
decides: Partly confirmed, because fopomonitor.com and mobilepixels.us returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today, so neither maker's compatibility statement was read. Using your record that the FOPO S1 is driver-free with two added screens, each screen needs its own native video output, so on an M2 MacBook Air (Apple: one external display) only one of the two would light. That consequence is my inference, not FOPO's statement. For that shopper the pick moves to a one-screen product: among partner items, the Mobile Pixels Fold 15.6" at $143.99 (your table, no record yet), or the ASUS ZenScreen MB169CK that ChatGPT showed, which ASUS lists with two USB-C DP Alt Mode ports and mini HDMI. For a Windows laptop with two video-capable outputs, the FOPO S1 through our link stays the two-added-screens row under $150. The Mobile Pixels Glance 16" at $151.99 (your table) sits just over the line. The page has its required two linked rows only if the Fold 15.6" gets a record, and both rows' video paths need a maker-page read before publishing.

findings.label: External displays an M2 MacBook Air drives
findings.value: 1 external display (up to 6K at 60 Hz), alongside the built-in display
findings.source_title: MacBook Air (M2, 2022) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's wording: 'One external display with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz'. Read for the 13-inch M2 Air only; I did not open the M1 or M3 spec pages.

findings.label: Apple's rule for MacBook Pro display count
findings.value: Depends on the Mac model and each display's resolution and refresh rate; Apple links one page per chip
findings.source_title: How many displays can be connected to MacBook Pro - Apple Support
findings.note: Page dated 2026-11-05. It gives no counts itself, only links to per-model pages.

findings.label: Video inputs (video path)
findings.value: 2 × USB-C (DP Alt Mode), 1 × mini HDMI; one added screen, freestanding
findings.source_title: ASUS ZenScreen MB169CK Tech Specs (ASUS USA)
findings.note: Native video, no driver named. The spec page carries no footnote on which laptop USB-C ports qualify beyond the '(DP Alt Mode)' label.

findings.label: Cables in the box and power draw
findings.value: USB-C cable, mini HDMI to HDMI cable, 360° kickstand, sleeve; no power adapter listed; 7.64 W power consumption
findings.source_title: ASUS ZenScreen MB169CK Tech Specs (ASUS USA)
findings.note: Also lists 250 cd/m² typical brightness and 0.78 kg net weight without stand. No price on this page; ASUS's store price was not read.

findings.label: What rank-1 rival says on compatibility
findings.value: Single-cable use needs a USB-C port with video output (DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt), otherwise HDMI plus a separate USB power cable; no DisplayLink, driver or MacBook chip limit mentioned
findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extenders Under $150 (2026) | The Office Journal
findings.note: Picks are Cevaton 15.6", KEFEYA 14", ROYY 14" and Miesebe 14", with no per-model video path or fit range. The page says it is based on published specifications, not hands-on testing.

findings.label: What dejaflow says on compatibility
findings.value: Per-model laptop fit ranges (e.g. SIAVIALA 14" '13–17.3 in'), DisplayLink driver required on SideTrak Slide, DP Alt Mode or mini HDMI on Mobile Pixels Duex Lite; no MacBook chip limit
findings.note: Its prices are dated 2026-02-16. Its text says 'plug-and-play laptop monitor extender for Mac and Windows, when your ports are ready'.

findings.label: What twelvetabs says on compatibility
findings.value: DisplayLink driver required on the Upperizon 15.6" dual ($309.99); fit ranges for two picks; no DisplayPort Alt Mode explanation and no MacBook chip limit
findings.source_title: Best Laptop Screen Extenders on Amazon (2026)
